spec.description: OHLC candles for one market, ending at `end` (or now, if omitted) and going back `limit` candles of `step` seconds each.

request.title: GetOhlcRequest
request.description: The market, candle width and how many candles to return.

start.description: Documented as the start of the range. Verified live to have no effect on the response when `end` is also sent -- see notes.

end.description: End of the range the newest returned candle is aligned to. Defaults to now.

exclude_current_candle.description: Whether to omit the current, still-open candle from the response. Defaults to `false`.

response.title: OhlcResponse
response.description: Wire frame; `pair` is kept alongside the candles rather than unwrapped, since it confirms which market answered.

data.title: OhlcData
data.description: The candles and the market they belong to.

pair.description: Display name of the market these candles are for, such as `BTC/USD`.

volume.description: Traded volume during the candle, in the base currency.

notes: No `pagination` block, despite `start`/`end`/`limit` looking like a `window` walk's parameters: called directly (a fixed `step`, an old, hour-aligned `start`/`end` pair, well clear of the live edge, per the authoring guide's own probing advice), `start` made no difference to the response at all -- with `end` and `limit` both set, the API returns exactly `limit` candles ending at `end` regardless of what `start` says, including when `start` is inside that span. A generated `window` walk advances `start` between requests; against this endpoint that walk would never converge; the request schema keeps `start` because the API accepts and documents it, and this note exists so nobody adds the block from the parameter names alone.

A market's `market_type` decides which key the frame uses for its name: this schema and every recorded example cover the `pair` key a spot market returns; a perpetual market (`btcusd-perp`) returns `market` instead of `pair` at the same position, and is out of scope here.
